g.text: An LLM, from training to your screen
Read it top to bottom. Letters are the model basics; numbers are the Day 1 speed cards. The key under the drawing links each one.
T ≈ Σ over N calls [ TTFT + (thinking tokens + answer tokens) ÷ output speed ] + tool time between calls
Done once, months before you ever call it. What comes out is a file of numbers.
guess the next token, trillions of times
Every wrong guess nudges the numbers a
little. Thousands of GPUs for months. Result:
a base model that continues any text.
Train further on example chats, then on which
answers people or automatic checkers prefer.
The base model becomes an assistant;
reasoning models learn to think first.
The model is this file of learned numbers plus a
fixed recipe (the architecture). Quantized to 4 bits
Copied into GPU memory and kept there. If it isn't
loaded yet, your first call waits for it: a cold
Left of the GPU is the wait before anything happens. The GPU does the work. Streaming brings it back.

KV cache: one note per token, and it grows as you go
Faster tokens: more bandwidth (hardware) · fewer bytes (quantization)
fewer weights per token (MoE) · more tokens per pass (speculative decoding)
Token ids → text, sent as each
are hidden, but you still wait
First word on screen = TTFT: network + queue + cold start
+ prefill + hidden thinking. After that, one token every
1 ÷ output speed: 653 tokens at 15.4 tok/s on your M3 is 42 s.
zoom in: what prefill and every decode step compute
The fixed recipe the weights plug into. Llama-3.1-8B's real sizes shown.
A lookup table with one row
Each token looks back at the earlier
ones and pulls in what's relevant. Their
keys and values are the KV-cache notes.
Reworks each token's numbers on its
own. Most of what a decode step reads
Prefill runs this recipe for every prompt token at once, so the math is the bottleneck. Decode runs it for one new token at a time,
so reading the 16 GB of weights each step is the bottleneck. That one difference explains most of the speed cards.
4 · The agent loop around it (Claude Code, Codex, …)
An agent makes the call in band 2 N times for one request. Everything that is per-call gets multiplied.
It either answers or asks for a
tool: read a file, run the tests,
The model waits, and so do you.
The tool result is appended. The next
call re-sends everything, so input piles
N calls means you feel the slow ones and the failures: 95% right per step is
